concern_results.conclusion: The nonzero add branch now invokes the verified release path before raising an error that names the abbreviated round head; no success path or acceptance token is changed.
Cleanup remains scoped to the run-created temporary path, removes the targeted worktree without repository-wide prune, and verifies registry removal before deleting any residual directory.

Both registered partial creation and failure before registration are handled coherently: surviving registration or directory state becomes a release problem, while an unregistered run-created directory is removed without a spurious complaint.

The added cases exercise the two relevant failure shapes and assert error output, absence of the success token, registry equality, and directory cleanup, but the bounded packet does not independently establish that they or the preceding 75 cases passed.
CLI compatibility is preserved except for an intentional appended cleanup diagnostic on creation failures; existing verdict tokens and successful behavior are untouched by the diff.
The implementation is confined to reversible error-path cleanup with no schema, migration, irreversible mutation, or deployment dependency.
Creation and cleanup failures are reported together, while successful cleanup preserves the original creation error without misleading release noise.

The shared release gate's acceptance path is unchanged and cleanup avoids affecting unrelated registrations, but release containment lacks independently verifiable full-suite execution evidence in the packet.
